name: Back Escape
description: Escape the back by winning the hand fight, slipping shoulder line, and turning to guard or top.
shortInstruction: Control the choking hand, drop the shoulder past their hip line, create one hook out, and turn into guard or stand up.
summary: Back escape requires winning the hand fight first, then creating space by dropping the trapped shoulder below the opponent's hip line. A systematic branch: hand fight → shoulder slip → single hook removal → turn or stand-up.
whyItWorks: Controlling the choking hand stops the primary finishing threat before you work on the escape
Dropping the shoulder below the hip line removes their primary structural control — the rib-to-back connection
Removing one hook at a time is more achievable than trying to shed both simultaneously
Turning into them rather than away reduces the risk of exposing the back again during the escape attempt
commonMistakes: Fighting the body triangle instead of the choking hand — you can survive the body triangle but not the choke
Turning away from the opponent (giving the other side of the neck) instead of turning into their chest
Using both hands on the choking hand and leaving the near hook completely uncontrolled
Waiting too long — the longer they have the back, the tighter their seatbelt and the harder the escape
safetySummary: The rear-naked choke comes on fast — if you feel the jaw line open, tap and reset before losing consciousness
Do not use explosive movements that might cause accidental spinal pressure when rolling from the back
If the opponent has a body triangle, prioritize breathing and hand fighting over panicked movement

systemLogic.corePrinciple: The back escape follows a four-step sequence: hand fight (control choking hand) → shoulder slip (drop trapped shoulder below hip line) → hook removal (clear one hook at a time) → turn or stand-up

decisionTree.action: Use both hands on their choking forearm, peel the arm away from the neck, keep it pinned to your chest
After controlling the arm, sit your hips away and drop the trapped shoulder past their hip line — this kills their seatbelt control

decisionTree.condition: They switch to an armbar attempt during the escape
decisionTree.action: Keep your elbows tight to your ribs and continue turning toward them

exitStrategies: If the escape fails and they re-establish back control, reset to the hand fight phase and start again
If they flatten you belly-down, protect your neck and use the wall/wrestling stand-up rather than rolling

moneyDetails: Back escapes win matches by denying 4 points to the opponent and returning to a neutral or advantageous position
A reliable back escape removes the fear of back control — you can take more risks entering scrambles
Competitors with strong back escapes are significantly harder to finish in tournaments
fixItFast: If you cannot reach the choking hand: trap their sleeve against your chest by hiding your chin and peeling with the opposite hand
If you remove one hook but they replace it immediately: keep the cleared leg posted wide and do not let it re-engage
If they flatten you belly-down from the back: protect your neck, get to your knees, and use the wall/wrestling stand-up rather than rolling
